full_judgment:
Md Anwarul Haque J: This Petition for Leave to Appeal, is directed against the judgment and order dated 1-3-2010 in discharging the Rule passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Misc. Case No.11907 of 2008 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure arising out of Metro Sessions Case No.2642 of 2007 corresponding to CR Case No.2488 of 2007 pending before the learned Joint Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka. 

 One Rahat Chowdhury, present respondent, filed a petition of complaint against the petitioner for committing the offence punishable under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 since the cheque issued by the accused-petitioner in favour of the Complainant-respondent to the tune of Taka 1,00;00,000 (one crore) has bounced for insufficient money in the account. On receipt of such complaint the learned magistrate in pursuance of the provision laid down in section 141 of the said Act, 1881 took cognizance of the offence punishable under section 138 of Act and sent the CR case No. 1488 of 2007 to the court of Sessions for trial. 

 3. During the course of trial the present-petitioner filed a petition for discharging the accused-petitioner under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure which was rejected and accused filed this Criminal Misc. Case under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of entire proceeding of the above Metro. Sessions Case No. 2642 of 2007 alleging that since it was an "account payee/cross cheque" it does not come within the mischief of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 but the learned Joint Sessions Judge rejected such prayer and proceeded with the trial where the High Court Division also endorsed the same view with the observation in detail that the provision laid down in section 123A(2)(a) has been wrongly interpreted in order to keep it within the ambit of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. 

 4. Mr Abdul Matin Khasru the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that "cross-cheque" or "account payee" cheque as has been mentioned in the compliant-petition does not come within the scope of section 138 of the Negotiable instruments Act,1881 because as soon as a cheque is made crossed it shall cease its negotiability. Mr Khashru has drawn our attention to the provision laid down in section 123A of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 which has been placed in Chapter XIV of the said Act in the name and style "Special Provisions Relating to Cheques" and accordingly when a cheque is crossed or made account-payee chequ6 it shall cease to be a Negotiable Instrument in the language employed in section 123A,(2)(a) of the Negotiable Instrument Act, 1881; as such the same cannot be brought within the mischief of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. In the instant case since it was a "cross-cheque" it cannot be a Negotiable Instrument; as such it does not come within the scope of section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. 

 6. In support of his contention the learned advocate has brought to our notice in the provisions laid down in section 13, 123A (2)(b) and section 126 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. Moreover, the words "any cheque" as has been employed in section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 clearly bring the cheque whether it is a "bearer" or "account payee" within the mischief of section 138 of the Act, 1881. In no way, it can be regulated by only the provisions laid down in section 123A(2)(a) rather, such "account payee" cheque is to be regulated by both sub-section (2)(a) and (b) of section 123A of the Negotiable Instruments Act. The provision laid down in section 123(2)(a) cannot be read or taken into consideration in an isolated manner rather the provision laid down in clause (b) is to be taken into consideration for the purpose of collection of money mentioned in the cheque. 

 13. In the light of the above discussion we are of the opinion that since the "account payee cheque" mentioned in the complaint-petition has not lost its character as Negotiable Instrument, the same can be easily brought within the mischief of "any cheque" employed in section 138(1) of the Negotiable Instruments Act because cheque includes "account payee cheque" also. So we find no substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and accordingly the petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.
